$comment: Gate B DRAFT rule object for RF-FIELD-002 — pending, NON-EXECUTABLE. Authored only from RF Clinical Rule Specification v1.2 §13.3 and the RF-FIELD-002 inventory entry. Mixed-source rule. Expresses the '95% maximum sprint speed is not sufficient alone' boundary only: reaching 95% MSS may contribute to Simulation evidence but cannot independently authorize unrestricted training or competition. 95% MSS is one field/sprinting data point within a broader multi-domain readiness model; it is not single-metric clearance, not proof of readiness, and clears no field domain it does not directly test. No dosage, sprint/running progression, exercise selection, field plan, complete rehab plan, RTT, or RTS logic; safety precedence preserved; does not bypass RF-FIELD-001, RF-RECUR-001/002, RF-REHAB-001..006, RF-SEV-005, RF-DX-006, or RF-SAF-006. Not approved. Not wired into any runtime.
rule_title: 95% maximum sprint speed is not sufficient alone

input_contract.$comment: The 95% MSS metric and its bounded role taken verbatim-in-meaning from v1.2 §13.3. It is one field data point within a broader readiness model; raw media is never interpreted here.

decision_contract.$comment: 95% MSS insufficiency boundary structure only. 95% MSS may contribute to Simulation evidence but cannot independently authorize unrestricted training or competition; it is not single-metric clearance, not readiness proof, and clears no untested field domain. No dosage, progression schedule, exercise selection, field/rehab plan, RTT, or RTS. Safety precedence preserved.

notes: Mixed normative source; MUST; permitted_use logic_with_uncertainty. Architecture refs preserved per source: V3.1-12 (current capacity & capacity-to-demand gap), V3.1-14.2 (tiered return-to-training & return-to-performance), V3.1-24 (confidence/evidence/output locks). Evidence grade/role preserved per source: QRF-025 (E1) preserved only in its source role — a multi-domain readiness restriction; it must NOT be generalized into unrestricted training/play authority, return-to-training/return-to-sport authority, or proof of readiness. Per §13.3 decision preserved exactly: reaching 95% maximum sprint speed may contribute to Simulation evidence but cannot independently authorize unrestricted training or competition. §13.3 does not enumerate additional companion evidence domains beyond 'Simulation evidence'; the companion-evidence requirement is therefore represented as the multi-domain Simulation/readiness model (V3.1 §14.2 and §24), NOT invented domains. 95% MSS is one field/sprinting data point only; it is not single-metric clearance, not proof of readiness, and clears no field domain it does not directly test (e.g. kicking, cutting, deceleration, change-of-direction, repeated sprinting, fatigue tolerance, sport-specific exposure) — consistent with RF-FIELD-001 and RF-RECUR-002. The rule creates no sprint/running progression schedule, dosage, work-to-rest ratios, exercise selection, complete field plan, complete rehab plan, RTT, or RTS, and never bypasses readiness-tier honesty, capacity-to-demand gap assessment, or symptom/monitoring/next-day response requirements. Safety-state choice (read §13.3 exactly): §13.3 does NOT assign a closed V3.1 safety state, so safety_state_output is null and blocked_targets is empty, and the insufficiency boundary is represented in decision_contract; no safety state was inferred by analogy. It does not bypass RF-FIELD-001, RF-RECUR-001/002, RF-REHAB-001..006, RF-SEV-005, RF-DX-006, or RF-SAF-006, and does not override RF-SAF-006, RF-DX-006, RF-DX-008, RF-SEV-004, RF-SEV-005, RF-RECUR-001, RF-RECUR-002, or RF-FIELD-001; uncertainty is preserved when MSS denominator quality, measurement method, test context, symptom/monitoring/next-day response, capacity, field-domain, schedule, or sport-demand evidence is incomplete. Running/sprinting boundary rule, not a safety rule. No field-exposure or readiness engine is authored here (deferred to the later field, rehab, and readiness objects). Draft — approval_status remains pending.
